Strategic Performance Drivers

The company is transitioning from a traditional retailer to an integrated omnichannel ecosystem where stores serve as high-velocity fulfillment nodes, with 80% of U.S. e-commerce orders now fulfilled from store locations.

Strategic growth is being driven by the "flywheel" effect of e-commerce momentum, which enables higher-margin commerce solutions like advertising and marketplace services to improve the overall business mix and profitability.

The new Walmart+ and Sam's Club Plus membership bundle aims to capture the "dual member" household, leveraging data that shows these customers are the most valuable and frequent shoppers despite being a small current cohort.

Marketplace growth of 49% is being sustained by expanding the product catalog and utilizing Walmart Fulfillment Services to provide same-day or next-day delivery for nearly 50% of marketplace GMV.

Management attributes significant share gains in grocery—the highest in three years—to aggressive price investments, including 7,700 active rollbacks and a holiday meal basket priced 12% lower than last year.

The "agentic commerce" initiative, centered on the Sparky shopping agent, is designed to reduce friction in the discovery process, with usage growth of 129% leading to 40% larger basket sizes.

Operational efficiency is being improved by scaling successful international innovations, such as China's "cloud warehouses" and India's "Flipkart Minutes," to optimize last-mile delivery speeds in the U.S. market.

Outlook and Guidance Assumptions

Full-year sales and earnings guidance was raised based on the assumption that year-to-date share gains and underlying sales trends will persist through a strong holiday season.

The fourth quarter is expected to benefit from a 100 basis point tailwind to sales growth due to the timing shift of Flipkart's Big Billion Days event in India.

Management expects continued pressure on Walmart U.S. comp sales from Maximum Fair Pricing (MFP) regulations, projected as a 125 basis point headwind, though it remains profit-neutral.

The company has expanded its restaurant delivery service to more than 2,700 locations. to improve last-mile density and driver utilization, viewing it as a natural extension to capture more meal occasions.

Long-term profitability is expected to benefit from the continued shift toward digital services, with e-commerce incremental margins targeted in the low double-digit range.

Walmart Inc (WMT) (Q3 2027) Earnings Call Highlights: Raised Guidance, 23% US E-Commerce Growth ...

This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

Enterprise Net Sales: Grew 4.4% in constant currency, exceeding guidance of 3%3.75%; faced ~100 bps headwind from Flipkart's Big Billion Days timing shift.

Walmart US Comp Sales: Up 2.9%, including ~70 bps headwind from health and wellness; 3.6% excluding health and wellness.

Sam's Club US Sales: Up 10%, with comps excluding fuel up nearly 5%.

International Sales: Grew over 3% in constant currency, with China up 28%, partially offset by Flipkart BBD timing.

E-commerce: Global net sales up 17%; Walmart US up 23% (11th consecutive quarter of 20%+ growth); Sam's Club up 30%; Canada and China each up more than 30%.

Grocery Sales: Up mid-single digits in Walmart US.

General Merchandise Sales: Up low single digits in Walmart US; GMV grew mid-single digits.

Marketplace & Fulfillment Services: Walmart US net sales up 49%, third consecutive quarter above 45%; nearly 50% of marketplace GMV flows through Walmart fulfillment services.

Advertising: US advertising (including VIZIO and Vibe) grew 37%; Walmart Connect up 36%.

Membership Fee Revenue: Grew 17% globally, led by double-digit Walmart+ growth in the US.

Adjusted Operating Income: Up 5.5% in constant currency; full-year guidance raised to 8%8.6% growth.

Adjusted EPS: Increased approximately 5%; full-year guidance raised to $2.84$2.89.

E-commerce Incremental Margins: Walmart US e-commerce achieved double-digit incremental margins.

Health & Wellness Impact: MFP regulation a ~125 bps comp headwind, partially offset by ~60 bps from higher GLP-1 sales.

Store-Fulfilled Deliveries: Up over 40%; expedited deliveries up more than 50%; stores fulfill over 80% of US e-commerce orders.

Delivery Network: Reaches 96% of US households in under three hours and 60% in under 30 minutes; delivery marketplace expanded to over 2,400 quick-service restaurant locations.

Price Investments: Approximately 7,700 rollbacks across US categories.

Debt Issuance: Approximately $6.5 billion in long-term debt issued at favorable rates.

Full-Year Sales Guidance: Raised to 4.9%5.2% growth (from 4%5%); Q4 implied growth of 4.5%5.5%.

Positive Points

Walmart Inc (NASDAQ:WMT) raised full-year sales and profit guidance, with enterprise sales growth now expected at 4.9%-5.2% and adjusted EPS of $2.84-$2.89.

Global e-commerce grew 17%, with US e-commerce up 23% and Sam's Club e-commerce up 30%, marking the 11th consecutive quarter of 20%+ growth in the US.

Walmart Inc (NASDAQ:WMT) is gaining market share, particularly in grocery, with food share gains the highest in three years, driven by price investments and faster delivery.

The new Walmart+ and Sam's Club Plus membership bundle launched in October 2026 is off to a strong start, with new member sign-ups and upgrades exceeding expectations.

Higher-margin businesses like advertising (US up 37%) and membership (fee revenue up 17%) are growing rapidly, improving overall profitability and supporting operating income growth faster than sales.
